o1.biggest_strength: It finds the real levers: courier silence, bra fit, and the refund-biased portal, then gives usable copy, sequencing, and sensible ranges with the maths shown.
o1.biggest_mistake: The exchange sales-kept number is a ceiling and could be read too confidently; I would label it more clearly as retained revenue at risk, not cost saving.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the revenue assumptions for swaps, add a clearer holdout/test plan by channel, and make sure the day-3 message handles no-scan parcels as well as scanned ones.

o2.biggest_strength: It is sharp on the main decision and gives honest, useful targets, especially by assuming only half the fit-finder gap is caused by the quiz.
o2.biggest_mistake: The day-3 update misses part of the main WISMO problem: if there is no courier scan by day 3, it sends the warehouse to check but does not clearly reassure the customer proactively.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a proactive no-scan customer message, include a post-delivery bra fit/swap nudge, remove the unnecessary Christmas/date assumptions, and make the delivered CTA point more directly to swapping when fit is wrong.

reason: I would rather hand Output 1 to the team tomorrow because it is more complete and closer to build-ready, with better coverage of the post-delivery fit moment. Output 2 is strong and a bit more cautious in places, but it leaves a bigger gap in the day-3 no-scan problem.
